implementation: Core lexical predicates expose complete Name and Lang spelling checks under a budget. They provide a shared contract for source-less constructors and printing without a Doc-to-reader dependency.

Name uses the existing pinned Unicode 16 XID tables with the NEPL underscore-start extension. The reader and reader-plan CharClass delegate to the same character predicates, retaining token boundaries and raw spelling.

Lang retains the existing RFC 5646 section 2.1 ABNF algorithm and Work accounting. Registry validity and duplicate variant/singleton restrictions are separate validity conditions, not silently introduced into lexical recognition.
unicode-ident remains version 1.0.18 with default features disabled; its direct dependency moves from reader to core. Cargo.lock and the dependency catalog describe the actual package owner.

independent_review.scope: Fixed Lexical12 only. No Docprinter or RegionQuery WIP. Old Lang full body equivalence plus actual public core and reader APIs on native/WASI.
independent_review.managed: core lexical3 and reader builtin17 independently passed native/WASI; tool transcript holds full cargo outputs. Root full gates separate.
independent_review.findings: No blocking finding. Native/WASI probes compare all 1,112,064 Unicode scalars against the existing pinned predicates and CharClass, compare old/new Lang results and budget usage, and exercise actual streaming reader boundaries. This checks extraction equivalence; it is not a new independent proof of Unicode property-table correctness.

sources.use: The standard distinguishes ABNF well-formedness from registry and duplicate-subtag validity.

log_normalization: Root logs use LF and a final newline. Archived independent UTF-8 records preserve original bytes and SHA-256.
